audit.whatIsWrong: content win[1] and win[2] give Levels 2 and 3 to Sion while whys[1] calls Level 2 'a slow farm lane with no real all-in from either side' and whys[2] says at 3 you sidestep his Q and punish. win[6] gives Two+ items to Sion while whys[6] and the late prose both say your item and Q scaling out-brawl his single-target kit.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is a charged, telegraphed cast on a 10s rank-1 cooldown; once The Darkin Blade is up every 10s and Umbral Dash every 7s, Aatrox re-arms faster than Sion's only trade tool. 54.3% over 2978 games.
audit.corrected: Level 2 evens to Skill, Level 3 and Levels 4-5 to Aatrox, Level 6 and First item stay Sion, Two+ items to Aatrox.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike says 'his knockup R plus E shield' and wants.foe[1] says 'Use E shield + Q'. Sion's shield is Soul Furnace, his W. His E is Roar of the Slayer. The spike also gives no cooldowns.
audit.why: Riot's text: Soul Furnace (W) 'Sion shields himself and can reactivate after 3 seconds to deal Magic Damage'; Roar of the Slayer (E) 'fires a short range shockwave that damages and slows and reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit'. Unstoppable Onslaught is 140/100/60 and Decimating Smash 10/9/8/7/6.
audit.corrected: Shield renamed to Soul Furnace (W, 15s) with its 3-second detonation; Roar of the Slayer named as the armour-shredding E; 140s R and 10s Q cooldowns added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interactions are absent. Soul Furnace is not just a shield — it re-detonates three seconds later for magic damage, so the shield IS the second half of his trade. Roar of the Slayer knocks a minion backwards through you, shredding armour along the line, which is how he lands damage without ever walking up. And Decimating Smash only knocks up and stuns when he charges it long enough.
audit.why: Riot's text on Q: 'If he charges for enough time, enemies hit by the swing will also be knocked up and stunned.' A short-charged Q is damage you can walk through; the fully-charged one is the only thing in his kit that stops your combo, and its wind-up is visible the whole time. Roar of the Slayer knocking minions through you means the safe spot is off the minion line, not just outside his Q cone.
audit.corrected: Charge-length condition on the Q stun, the Soul Furnace re-detonation, and the minion-knockback line of Roar of the Slayer now stated in spikes[0], spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says stacking armour is the wrong answer here.
audit.why: Soul Furnace's detonation and Glory in Death's attacks both scale on maximum health rather than being answered by resistances, so armour buys much less against Sion than against a normal AD top. Roar of the Slayer additionally shreds the armour you did buy.
audit.corrected: Stated in the full-layer tldr rather than inventing a new item line.

edits.before: Your kill window: bait his Q charge, sidestep it, then land Q3 sweetspot into W chain and drain him down. His whole trade hinges on the slow Q — dodge it and he has nothing.
edits.after: Your kill window: only a long-charged Decimating Smash stuns, so read the wind-up, leave the cone, then Q3 sweetspot into chain and drain. Dodge that 10s Q and he has nothing.

edits.before: Sion 6 gets R Unstoppable Onslaught — a global-ish charge that flips fights. Don't get pinned against a wall; his knockup R plus E shield can turn your all-in into his kill.
edits.after: Sion 6 gets Unstoppable Onslaught (140s), a steered charge that flips fights. Don't fight near a wall: R knockup into a Soul Furnace that re-pops 3s later kills you.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are yours. Sion's entire trade pattern revolves around landing his slow Q — sidestep it and he's a sitting duck for your Q3 sweetspot into W Infernal Chains and drain. Force trades when his Q is down; two points in Q plus your passive heal beats his shield sustain. Be careful at 6: his R Unstoppable Onslaught flips fights and tips that window to him, so never fight with your back to a wall where he can pin and knock you up.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are yours. Only a fully-charged Decimating Smash stuns, so read the wind-up, leave the cone, and he is a sitting duck for Q3 into Infernal Chains and drain. Fight in his 10s Q gap, and stand off the minion line — Roar of the Slayer knocks a minion back through you and shreds your armour. Remember Soul Furnace re-detonates 3s after he shields. At 6 never fight with your back to a wall.

edits.before: Use E shield + Q to win extended fights
edits.after: Soul Furnace shield into its 3s pop dmg

edits.before: Late-game your item and Q scaling out-brawl his single-target threat.
edits.after: Late your items out-brawl him, but armour is wrong against Sion.

edits.before: Sion changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Sion charged Q, W, E, R, and passive. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Sion wants to survive lane, farm safely, stack durability, and become more valuable in later fights than the early lane suggests.
edits.after: Sion changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect a Decimating Smash that only stuns when charged long, and Soul Furnace re-detonating 3s after it shields. Aatrox wins by reading that wind-up, spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, and fighting in the 10s Q gap. Armour is the wrong buy — Soul Furnace and Glory in Death both scale on health, and Roar of the Slayer shreds what you bought.

edits.before: Sion charged Q, W, E, R, and passive
edits.after: Charged Q stun, Soul Furnace pop 3s
